title: Scalar-restriction resolutions are quasi-isomorphisms on sections of every slice
statement: Let C : Type a be a category with arrows in Type v, let J be a Grothendieck topology, and set m=max(a,v,r). Assume J admits composition with the commutative-ring forgetful functor, abelian sheafification in universe m, and its locally bijective characterization. Let B,D be sheaves of rings in universe m whose multiplication is commutative on each object, and b:B→D a ring-sheaf map. For K-injective cochain complexes I of D-module sheaves and K of B-module sheaves, every quasi-isomorphism j:Res_b(I)→K induces a quasi-isomorphism of the underlying abelian-group complexes of sections on each object U of C.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, on the slice over an object; literature/stacks-project/sites-modules.tex, Tags 03DI and 03DJ, exact extension by zero and restriction to a slice.

proof.text: Retain commutativity on the given ring sheaves without changing their ring data. Lift the ring homomorphism to the fully faithful commutative-ring forgetful functor. Restrict the two complexes and the resolution map to the slice over U. Exact restriction preserves the quasi-isomorphism; its exact left adjoint shows that it preserves K-injective complexes.

Apply scalar-restriction acyclicity of global sections on the slice. The slice has terminal object id_U. The natural isomorphisms from global sections to the limit and to evaluation at this terminal object identify the resulting map with the original sections of j on U. Quasi-isomorphisms are invariant under this natural isomorphism.
